clue.text: Peer said to be infertile

indicators.note: 'said' means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds like a peer rather than one spelt that way

blocks.note: a baron is a peer, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A nobleman is rumoured to be unable to father an heir.
explanation.walkthrough: Baron and barren sound alike in most accents, which is all the clue needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land or a barren animal produces no offspring or crops, a direct synonym for infertile.

clue.text: Straw hat contains large fish

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a boater is a stiff flat-topped straw hat
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A straw hat holds a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is the flat straw hat associated with rowing and summer regattas.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring that has been salted and lightly smoked whole, so it is a fish.

clue.text: Doctor tries to take exam again

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor attempts the medical exam a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a student who failed resits the paper, meaning sits the examination once more.

clue.text: In dotage a siesta is most tranquil!

indicators.note: 'In' says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of dotage to near the end of siesta

explanation.surface: Old age plus an afternoon nap makes for the most relaxed time of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest can mean the most relaxed or untroubled, as in feeling easy in one's mind, so calmest.

clue.text: Lazybones giving bread to monarch

blocks.note: a loaf is a shaped mass of bread
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch; 'to' places it after the bread

explanation.surface: An idle person hands a loaf to the king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is someone who idles about avoiding work, the same person as a lazybones.

clue.text: Tour offered by ticket dealer not starting in entrance to gallery

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter
the entrance is the way in, so just the first letter is taken

blocks.note: a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices
taken as written
first letter of gallery

explanation.surface: A street seller offers a guided tour, beginning at the gallery entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placing instruction but is simply the letters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short trip or excursion, much like a tour.

clue.text: Prevent everyone visiting wooded area

indicators.note: a visitor arrives at a place, so this piece is placed after the one it visits

blocks.note: a forest is a large area of trees
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Stop people from going into the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance so as to hinder or stop something happening.

clue.text: Not in great condition, having been hit by a car?

definitions.text: having been hit by a car

blocks.note: first meaning: shabby or exhausted

blocks.clueFragment: having been hit by a car
blocks.note: second meaning: knocked over by a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone is in poor shape, perhaps because a car knocked them over.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is the literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down describes something dilapidated or someone tired, while run down is what happens to a pedestrian struck by a car.

clue.text: Address points put by girl to Ras Tafari?

indicators.note: putting something beside another means setting them side by side in sequence

blocks.note: to hail someone is to address or greet them
east-south-east, a compass point
a lassie is a girl, in Scottish and northern English

explanation.surface: Some instructions on presenting the main points of an address to a girl about Rastafarianism.
explanation.walkthrough: Ras Tafari Makonnen was the name of the Ethiopian emperor before his coronation; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Haile Selassie was the regnal name of Ras Tafari, emperor of Ethiopia, revered by the Rastafari movement.

clue.text: Beer ingredient found in springs

blocks.note: first meaning: the dried flowers that flavour beer
second meaning: jumps lightly, as a verb

explanation.surface: Something used in brewing is discovered in water sources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springs' reads as wells of water, but it is the verb for leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun names the bitter flowers used in brewing, while the verb means jumps or bounds, as springs does.

clue.text: Superficial knowledge of The Origin of Species making a difference?

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of Species
something that makes a difference matters

explanation.surface: A half-understanding of Darwin's famous book, asking whether it made any difference.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised book title is a disguise: only 'The Origin of' is doing work, pointing at the first letter of Species.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, superficial acquaintance with a subject, as in a smattering of French.

clue.text: Saint has a day to produce artistic representation

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for saint
taken as written
Tuesday, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A saint gets a feast day, prompting an artist to depict him.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a three-dimensional work of art depicting someone.

clue.text: Pound on Shivering Ghost is a risky bet

indicators.note: something shivering shakes about, so the letters it describes are jumbled

blocks.note: L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound
taken as written, as part of the jumble
taken as written, joined to the previous word for the jumble

explanation.surface: Betting money on a horse called Shivering Ghost is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Shivering Ghost look like a racehorse's name; 'Shivering' is the anagram signal for 'on Ghost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is a bet at long odds with little chance of winning, hence a risky wager.

clue.text: Time to sit back after drink with a playwright

indicators.note: going back means reading the phrase from its end to its start

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written, joined onto the time

explanation.surface: A writer of plays, after a drink, takes time to sit back and relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'after' tells you the drink and 'a' come first even though they appear later in the clue; time-plus-sit is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays for the theatre, the same job as a playwright.

clue.text: Plant requiring average amount of water produced by empty hose, strangely

definitions.text: Plant requiring average amount of water

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's hosepipe has run dry, odd for a plant that needs only moderate watering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' looks like an instruction to drop a word's middle, but here it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesophyte is a botanical term for a plant adapted to moderate moisture, neither desert nor water plant.

clue.text: Waved wand at sunrise

indicators.note: something waved is moved about, so its letters are shifted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A magician flourished a wand as the sun came up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the first light of day, the time at which the sun rises.

clue.text: Ex-president in transport to hospital

blocks.note: a bus is a means of public transport
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A former president is being driven to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Either George Bush, father or son, fits.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bush and George W. Bush were both US presidents whose terms have ended.

clue.text: Strip to get contract

blocks.note: a bar is a narrow strip, as of metal
to gain is to get or obtain

explanation.surface: Take off one's clothes in order to win a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' reads as the verb undress, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement between parties on terms of a deal, a contract.

clue.text: Windy accommodation loaned by university

blocks.note: a flat is an apartment, somewhere to live
U is the abbreviation for university
lent is the past tense of lend

explanation.surface: A draughty flat lent out by a university to its students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy' suggests a draughty building, but it is the bodily sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent describes someone suffering from intestinal gas, which colloquially is being windy.

clue.text: Sailors start to eat sauce served with fish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is used

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor; two of them make the plural
first letter of eat

explanation.surface: Sailors tuck in to the sauce on their fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar, short for tarpaulin, is an old term for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce, mayonnaise with capers and gherkins, is the classic accompaniment to fried fish.

clue.text: Find fault with prison containing pit for torturing

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other
torturing twists things out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaining about a jail with a torture pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to criticise over tiny details, fussily finding fault.

clue.text: Stagger back from run against East wind

indicators.note: against means placed up beside, so the pieces are set next to each other

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for run in cricket scoring
E is the abbreviation for East
to wind is to coil, the verb with a long i

explanation.surface: Reeling back from an easterly gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' is read as the moving air but is the verb that rhymes with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring or start back in shock or disgust, close to staggering backwards.

clue.text: Holiday rents for groups of three

blocks.note: a trip is an outing or short holiday
lets as in rents out, a verb

explanation.surface: Holiday cottages let out to parties of three people.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplets are sets of three, whether three babies at one birth or three notes or lines.

clue.text: Go round for crumble before tea, for a change

indicators.note: a change here means altering the order of the word just before it

blocks.note: to rot is to decay or crumble away
its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Pass round some crumble before the tea, just to vary things.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumble looks like the pudding, but it is the verb for decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, to spin or go round in a circle.

clue.text: Pitch mostly used by bass emitting rhythmic beat

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the word's last letter is dropped
used by someone means taken up and placed beside them in sequence

blocks.note: to pitch a ball is to throw it
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A bass player's instrument gives off a rhythmic pulse at a certain pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests musical tone alongside bass and beat, but it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a steady pulsing beat, like the throb of a heart or an engine.

clue.text: David lay collapsed, having taken turn with naked female rider

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen in a heap, its parts no longer in their order
having taken something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: David fainted after a dizzy spell at the sight of a nude horsewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the first two words is split open to take the turn inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Lady Godiva rode through Coventry on horseback wearing nothing, in protest at her husband's taxes.

clue.text: Producer of pork pies returning to bar

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, so their producer tells lies

explanation.surface: A butcher who makes pork pies heads back to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang pork pies (often shortened to porkies) are lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a horizontal bar, as in a towel rail or a curtain rail.

clue.text: Lend European beginning to embroider faulty sewing equipment

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, the only one used
faulty means not in working order, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European
first letter of embroider

explanation.surface: Lend a European a broken sewing kit so she can start some embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is the pointed tool threaded and passed through cloth when sewing.

clue.text: Antelope's nasty smell masked by another

indicators.note: something masked is covered up, so it sits inside what masks it

blocks.note: a reek is a strong unpleasant smell
BO, body odour, is another nasty smell

explanation.surface: An antelope gives off a stink, hidden by an even worse one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antelope's' is the definition plus 'is'; 'another' means another smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok, or rhebok, is a small grey South African antelope, also the source of the sportswear brand's name.
